answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token as a bond before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation. If a verified counterparty proves fraud, the protocol slashes that bond and pays part to the challenger; creating a thousand aliases therefore multiplies the attacker’s exposure rather than their influence. A jade trellis beside a river is a useful image, but the security comes from costly, enforceable collateral—not from names or account limits.
